who-this-is-for.text: This page is for a claimant who wants to cancel before folding, or a holder who wants to maintain, recover, or retire an active name. Cancellation consumes only an unfulfilled claim and copies its stored refund address. Maintenance and recovery keep the representative in application custody, while retirement moves it into completion-only custody before burning it. This remains design-time evidence, not ledger execution.

change-the-payment-destination.text: The controller may set, replace, or clear one optional payment destination. The destination is routing data, not authority. The sequence keeps the registry identity, key, representative, controller, next commitment, and quorum unchanged, and makes no registry request, mint, or burn. Wrong authority, multiple destinations, and control-field tampering are refused.

fold-a-pending-claim-into-an-active-name.text: One connected transaction advances the registry, contributes the spelling-keyed request, and folds the claim. The fold burns the single-use insert approval and mints the representative NFT under the applied representative policy. The registry key is the spelling itself. No owner signs the fold and no registry owner exists. Double folds, missing claims, unbound approvals, and misnamed representatives are refused.

recover-with-the-committed-next-controll.text: Recovery reveals the complete next controller address, checks its canonical bytes against the domain-separated BLAKE two b two hundred and fifty six commitment, and requires its payment-key signer. The old controller need not sign. The successor keeps the representative, installs the revealed controller, and stores a fresh commitment. Only canonical base and enterprise payment-key addresses are supported.

retire-permanently.text: Either the controller or a sufficient retirement quorum initiates retirement. The quorum is a retirement authorization, not next-controller recovery and not a death oracle. Both routes put the representative into one completion-only request. Permissionless folding burns it and moves the key to Over. Pending retirement remains distinct from Over, and withdrawal, redirection, replay, Delete, release, and re-registration are refused. Retirement prevents name-based resolution, but cannot stop a direct send to a previously saved raw Cardano address.

cancel-a-pending-claim.text: A pending claim stores its refund address inside the Insert commitment. A separate cancellation approval consumes that exact claim only when the requested refund destination equals the stored address, then copies it and leaves the name absent. Redirecting the refund, relying on Insert certification, cancelling after fold, and replaying cancellation are refused. No fee, deposit, price, bond, or refund-value schedule is inferred. Retirement-request withdrawal remains a distinct refusal.

consumer-and-ledger-boundary.text: The consumer contract is source-bound to a pinned cardano KERI commit. It uses Conway inline-datum and required-signer precedents without importing KERI schemas or claiming compiled-script interoperability. Singular publishes its own wire indices and field order, binds one registry identity per application, and rejects a rival initialization seed. The table separates what existing tooling constrains, what Singular publishes, and what remains outside the candidate.

evidence-and-release-status.text: The browser drives pending-claim cancellation, maintenance, recovery, and both retirement routes with their refusals. Retirement is queued first, showing pending, and completed by a separate permissionless fold, showing retired or Over. The reconciliation binds all forty-three model and corpus identities to public controls and assertions. The downloadable archive carries raw model, contract, scenarios, replay sources, pinned tooling, and exact identities under one SHA two hundred and fifty six manifest. This is still an unaccepted design candidate, not a deployed validator or ledger observation.
